jobs.title: Senior Product Owner, Support Platform & AI
jobs.description:
About Jimdo
 
 We exist to unleash the power of the self-employed - helping solopreneurs and micro-businesses thrive by doing what they're passionate about and removing the complexity of building lasting, successful businesses.
 Jimdo started in 2007 when three school friends built a website builder in a Northern German farmhouse to help everyone build a presence online. Today, we're a profitable, remote-first company with 220+ people from 50+ nationalities working across 15+ countries. We've helped build over 36 million websites to get online across the world.
 We're more than just a website builder. We're an AI-powered platform that helps self-employed people actually run and build successful businesses — from getting found online, winning customers and running their business with a peace of mind by knowing exactly what to do next to move forward.
 At the heart of Jimdo is a strong belief in personalized, data-driven guidance. Our platform combines design, business tools, and an AI-powered core that turns real customer data into clear insights and next steps helping our customers focus on what moves their business forward.
 
 Role Overview 
 At Jimdo, we think the best support is the one a customer never needs. When our customers, self-employed people and small business owners, do need help, it should come fast: from self-service and AI first, and from a person when that's what the case needs.
 We're bringing our support tooling, Zendesk, chatbots and AI work together into one team with one backlog and one roadmap. As Senior Product Owner, you'll lead that team and own the outcome: more questions answered by AI, faster help, lower cost to serve, and customers who still trust us.
 You'll also shape where this goes next. Over the next couple of years AI will handle more and more first-line support, and you'll decide how the work is split between AI and people, and build the platform around it.
  
 The team and who you'll work with 
 You'll report to the Head of Customer Support Services and join CSS, our support organisation.
 You'll lead a small team of Zendesk and AI specialists and work day to day with the engineers who build our support tools.
 You'll work closely with our knowledge and readiness team, support agents and team leads, product teams, our Company AI team, Data & Analytics, and our support and AI vendors.
  
 What you'll be doing: 
 Set the vision for our support platform and AI with the Head of CSS, and turn it into a roadmap, a business case and results.

 Lead, coach and grow your team, and bring specialists and engineers together around one backlog and clear quarterly outcomes.

 Own how well our chatbot, Zendesk AI agents and Copilot perform: define what a good AI answer is, measure it, and switch off what doesn't help customers.

 Improve routing, user identification and self-service entry points so customers get to the right answer faster.

 Spend real time with customers and support agents: read tickets, listen to chats, see where people get stuck.

 Build a written case for every bigger piece of work, own the cost to serve, and check results against your forecast.

 Turn what you learn in support into evidence that helps product teams fix problems at the source.

 
 Your first months 
 After 3 months: your team works from one backlog and one outcome roadmap, and the quality bar for AI answers is agreed.

 After 6 months: you've delivered and reported your first quarterly outcome, including how AI resolution compares with your forecast.

 
 What you bring to the table
 5+ years as a Product Owner or Product Manager, ideally including support, CX, service or internal platform products.

 You've shipped AI or chatbot features in production and can name the metric you moved, the baseline and the result.

 You explain product decisions in commercial terms: cost, savings, effect, and what you learned when a forecast was wrong.

 You've managed people and led people who didn't report to you, ideally across departments.

 You do your own analysis with SQL or BI tools, and design and read experiments without waiting for an analyst.

 A clear point of view on what a good support experience is, and fluent English for everyday work.

 Nice to have
 Hands-on experience with Zendesk (or a similar tool such as Intercom or Salesforce Service Cloud), including AI agents, routing and automations.

 Experience using support insights to change a product team's roadmap.

 German language skills.

 
 What we offer:
 
 Inspiring Mission: At our core, we are driven by a meaningful mission - to  empower solopreneurs and small businesses to succeed and  to contribute to the sustainability and vibrancy of the communities they serve.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description:
P-1345

You will be the Product Manager for the Databricks Runtime team in Berlin. The team works at the intersection of query processing, storage, infrastructure and data governance, all key components of the Databricks data intelligence platform. As the Product Manager, you will develop a deep understanding of modern cloud infrastructure, data governance solutions, and open source components, and gather requirements from customers. You will launch features that will impact how customers process petabytes of data every day and make it simpler for them to draw value from their data. 

This role requires coordinating all product activities from vision to implementation, including engaging customers to understand their needs, developing long-term product strategy, defining product roadmaps, working with engineering to build those products, and coordinating with various internal stakeholders (both pre- and post-launch) to ensure product success.

The impact you will have:

  • Own the end-to-end product management process
  • Gather customer requirements, design features and collaborate with engineering to deliver a polished market-ready product
  • Drive launches with product marketing through blog posts, release notes, webinars
  • Define and measure OKRs for your products
  • Drive the prioritization and development of features, measurably making it simpler and more cost effective for customers to govern and process petabytes of data.

What we look for:

  • 6+ yrs of experience
  • Bachelors degree in Computer Science or similar field
  • Experience in Product Management (inbound, outbound, cross-functional processes)
  • Technical skills
  • Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Strong data analysis and operationalization skills (SQL, rollups, building operational dashboards)

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and Instagram.

 We are looking for a Terminology Project Manager to join the Medical Excellence team in Berlin. 
 As a Terminology Project Manager, your mission will be to contribute to the delivery of medical initiatives with a direct public health impact. Working closely with our Global Medical Data Program Manager, you will play a pivotal role in revolutionising healthcare through the power of data — driving our mission to transform medical data management and interoperability in Germany.
 This is a full time position with a one year contract (parental leave replacement).
 
 What you’ll do 
 Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:
 Deliver adjusted terminologies to support new product launches and features

 Build comprehensive terminologies for both patients and healthcare professionals, ensuring unified workflows across our products

 Develop tools (Python programs and AI prompts) to support your work

 Collaborate with external medical experts to validate the relevance and usability of chosen terminologies

 Analyse product manager needs and work closely with Tech teams to understand technical constraints

 Write terminology documentation and communicate on your work across stakeholders

 
 Who you are 
 Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.
 You could be our next team mate if you have:
 Experience in Data and Interoperability Projects: experience in data, terminology or interoperability projects in Germany. Whether you are an expert or have a strong project management background, your experience will be invaluable in driving our projects forward.

 Experience in the Medical field: you have a medical background from medical studies or a previous experience in a medical company.

 Structured and Analytical Mindset: You thrive in structured environments and possess a strong analytical mindset. Your ability to break down complex problems and develop effective solutions will be instrumental in ensuring the success of our medical data initiatives.

 Detail-Oriented and Inquisitive: You have a keen eye for detail and enjoy delving deep into topics. Your meticulous approach will ensure the accuracy and quality of our medical data management processes.

 Result and Action-Oriented: You are driven by results and possess strong project management skills. Your ability to set clear goals, prioritize tasks, and drive projects to completion will be essential in achieving our objectives.

 User-Centric : You genuinely care about the end-users of your work. By putting the needs of our users at the forefront, you will contribute to the development of user-centric medical data solutions that enhance the healthcare experience.

 Excellent Communication Skills : Your exceptional communication skills enable you to effectively collaborate with teams from diverse backgrounds, including medical professionals, software developers, and data scientists. You are able to articulate complex technical challenges in simple terms.

 Fluent in German and English : You are fluent in both German and English, enabling you to communicate effortlessly in both languages. Proficiency in Italian or French is a plus, further enhancing your ability to collaborate with a diverse team.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

CreateFuture is a Version 1 company and AI-native consulting partner where people do work that matters and are supported to do it well. We work alongside organisations such as PayPal, adidas, NatWest, FanDuel and Money Saving Expert, building digital products and services that make a difference  while always putting people first.

We’re a team of creators. We write code, shape delivery, build go-to-market strategies, develop AI solutions and create the practices that support our people. We work side by side with our clients, challenging what’s not working and helping them to build the future. Our commitment to craft, quality, and culture has helped us scale to over 600 people in just a few years.

Our UK Benefits 

  • 35 days leave (including bank holidays). 
  • Private medical insurance.
  • Enhanced parental and adoption leave. 
  • Financial coaching + 5% pension match.
  • 40 hours of paid learning and development.

 View our full list of UK benefits.

CreateFuture is a Great Place to Work-Certified™ company and has won Best Workplaces UK multiple years in a row.

Join us on our journey. Let’s create tomorrow, together, today.

The Role

CreateFuture are looking for a collaborative and pragmatic Lead Product Manager to join our growing team and help us define and develop an exciting array of products over a variety of industries, technologies and domains.

Our Product Managers are responsible for working with senior leadership, our internal design and engineering teams and our clients to help define and implement product strategies that are consistent with our clients’ vision. This can be from early stage research and market analysis through to development, delivery and iteration.

As we rapidly scale, we’ve identified an exciting opportunity for a Lead Product Manager to help support our growth. 

This person will be responsible for shaping and leading client engagements. We have a variety of clients across many industries all of whom look to us to provide leadership and guidance.  

You will rapidly gain their trust and guide them toward a valuable customer focused outcome. To do this you’ll use your deep understanding of product management methodologies and a consistent application of good practice. 

You will also be responsible for the wellbeing of a team of product managers. You will help embed good practice and coach your team in client management techniques and the application of product management. 

Does this sound like you? Do you have experience in developing Product Managers and a passion for the craft of Product Management? Do you have an empathetic leadership style with a focus on coaching each person to help grow their career and skills? If so, we’ve got a great role for you to stretch your wings and see what you’re really capable of.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Reporting into the Head of Product Operations and be able to represent the team as we grow
  • Leading a team of Product Managers and support recruitment 
  • Helping embed and support career progression pathways using our development framework for personal growth
  • Providing support to the team through mentorship and coaching
  • Acting as an escalation point for the team, helping to remove internal and external blockers as needed
  • Supporting resourcing of Product Managers on projects
  • Identifying training and development needs
  • Lead clients through their digital transformation journey, ensuring long term lasting relationships are made with key decision-makers

jobs.title: Senior AI Product Manager - Platform
jobs.description:
About Zego 🚀 
 At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

 We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖
 For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

 Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor .

 
 If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring. 
 
 About the Role 
 We are looking for a Senior AI Product Manager to join our Platform team. Platform powers every customer journey at Zego: the core services behind quoting, buying, paying for, changing, renewing and cancelling a policy.
 You’ll own a product domain within Platform, defining its quarterly strategy and goals and helping refine the longer-term platform strategy as we rebuild and modernise some of Zego’s most critical services. You’ll turn technical challenges into business value, and make sure your services are resilient, compliant and ready to be used by AI agents as well as our apps.
 
 What You’ll Be Doing 
 Define your domain’s quarterly strategy and goals , and help refine the longer-term plans for Platform, balancing new capability, legacy rebuilds and reliability.

 Lead complex discovery autonomously as we modernise the policy lifecycle, moving capability off legacy systems one safe slice at a time.

 Dive deep into technical detail , understanding dependencies and failure modes, and making informed trade-offs with engineering.

 Treat internal teams as your customers , so launching a new product, price or journey on the platform is fast and predictable.

 Make your services AI-ready , with clean, well-documented APIs and data that agents and automations can use safely, and establish AI-enabled workflows for your domain.

 Put the right metrics in place , from reliability and incidents to time-to-launch and cost to serve, and build the business case for platform investment.

 Build compliance in from day one with Legal, Compliance and Finance, so money flows and customer communications are accurate and auditable.

 Bring stakeholders along , running ceremonies with senior stakeholders, facilitating big-room planning and knowing when to escalate.

 
 What You’ll Need to Be Successful 
 Platform product ownership. A track record of owning a technical, platform or backend product domain and delivering material business impact in a high-growth environment.

 Technical literacy. Confident with engineers on system architecture, APIs, event-driven services and workflow orchestration. Ideally, you come from engineering or data science.

 Legacy modernisation. You’ve led incremental rebuilds of business-critical services while keeping the lights on.

 Data and commercial fluency. You use financial, behavioural and usage data to ground decisions, query Snowflake or Looker yourself, and can build the case for platform investment.

 Clarity in complexity. You untangle dependencies across multiple business domains and explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders.

 Regulated environment. Ideally, experience in insurance, payments, lending or financial services, with compliance built into product design.

 You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.

 
 The Zego ways of working 🏡 
 Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.
 We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.
 Here is what the last one looked like .
 
 Benefits 🎁 
 💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.
 🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.
 📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build
 🩺 Private me

 Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Product team defines how millions of people experience Deliveroo, turning complex marketplace challenges into simple, high-impact solutions.

 We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our London team. In this role, you'll help us expand our on-demand grocery and retail offering, building a trusted shopping experience that customers rely on for their everyday local commerce needs.

 

 What You'll Be Doing 

 You'll be joining the New Verticals team. New Verticals is Deliveroo's business for on-demand grocery and retail: expanding what customers can buy on Deliveroo beyond restaurants, from everyday essentials to products from well-known brands and local stores. It's a key growth area for the company, focused on building a trusted, repeatable shopping experience.

 Partner with Customer Research to uncover barriers to transaction and translate those insights into high-conviction growth bets.

 
 Design and run controlled experiments to understand how affordability and selection influence behaviour, validating hypotheses through data.

 
 Drive alignment and trade-offs by balancing customer experience with unit economics and marketplace dynamics, communicating clearly to senior stakeholders.

 
 
 What You'll Need to Thrive

 Proven ability to solve complex problems, with a knack for asking the right questions and translating ambiguity into actionable roadmaps.

 
 High analytical fluency and significant experience being data-savvy, with the ability to diagnose performance drivers and partner effectively with Data Science.

 
 Demonstrated ownership of high-velocity execution, maintaining a sharp eye for detail in an environment where impact is paramount.

jobs.description:
Product Manager, Device Data Management (Français/Anglais) 
 Lieu : Paris, France (hybride, trois jours par semaine au bureau)
 Niveau : Senior Product Manager
 Équipe : Device Data Management (DDM)
 Contrat : CDI
 À noter : ce poste est basé en France. Vous devez donc y résider ou être prêt·e à déménager, et disposer déjà du droit de travailler dans l’UE. Nous ne pouvons pas proposer de sponsoring de visa, mais nous l’examinons poste par poste : gardez un œil sur notre site carrières pour les opportunités à venir. 
 Un français et un anglais courants (à l’oral comme à l’écrit) sont indispensables, et nous vous demandons de soumettre votre CV en anglais . À propos de Kaluza 
 Kaluza est la plateforme d’Energy Intelligence qui transforme la complexité de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les acteurs de l’énergie à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.
 Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel à travers les foyers, les appareils, les marchés et les réseaux. En combinant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie quotidienne.
 Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des innovateurs comme Volvo et Volkswagen.
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 Vous serez responsable de la localisation française de Device Data Management (DDM), l’un des domaines produit clés de la plateforme Kaluza. DDM consomme des flux de données internes et externes pour représenter les fournitures, compteurs, registres, relevés et consommations. Il gère aussi les parcours liés à ces entités (par exemple, la mise à jour de la configuration d’un compteur), les API qui exposent les données, les pages front-end qui les présentent aux utilisateurs, ainsi que les calculs de projection et d’extrapolation de consommation. C’est un rôle produit full-stack et très opérationnel : vous interviendrez sur tout le domaine, du modèle de données jusqu’à ce que voient les utilisateurs à l’écran.
 Traduire les exigences du marché français en spécifications claires : transformer les règles du marché de l’énergie français (Enedis, GRDF, passerelle GRD, règles sur les données de compteurs et d’équipements) en exigences produit détaillées couvrant la conformité réglementaire, les flux de données des équipements et la qualité des données.

 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec nos clients : collaborer main dans la main avec ENGIE et les futurs clients du marché français pour comprendre leurs besoins et construire les exigences ensemble. Bâtir une relation de confiance telle qu’ils viennent vous voir en premier, et vous appuyer sur cette proximité pour orienter ce que DDM construira ensuite pour la France.

 Construire, pas seulement spécifier : passer vous-même de l’idée au prototype fonctionnel en interrogeant les données, en esquissant des contrats d’API et en montant des preuves de concept. Nous attendons de vous que vous utilisiez quotidiennement des outils d’IA (ex. Claude Code) comme multiplicateur pour prototyper, investiguer et débloquer des situations, et pas seulement pour rédiger des documents.

 Aligner les équipes globales et locales, toutes fonctions confondues : travailler étroitement avec l’ingénierie, l’UX, la QA et bien d’autres, avec une influence full-stack, pour que tout le monde vise les bons résultats.

 Être la personne de référence pour DDM France : faire le lien entre nos équipes globales et locales afin d’éclairer les priorités et la stratégie.

 Ce que vous apportez : 
 Critères essentiels :
 Une expérience avérée en tant que Product Manager, Business Analyst ou équivalent dans des éditeurs de logiciels, avec un solide historique de localisation réussie de produits logiciels complexes pour des marchés internationaux

 Un français courant et une grande aisance en anglais : notre plateforme et beaucoup de nos équipes fonctionnent en anglais, vous passez donc facilement de l’un à l’autre

 De l’aisance dans le travail direct avec les clients : vous savez animer une session de travail avec des interlocuteurs clients, faire émerger le vrai besoin derrière la demande, et garder les décideurs alignés et impliqués

 Un état d’esprit de bâtisseur et une aisance technique : débrouillard·e et opérationnel·le, vous préférez construire un prototype fonctionnel plutôt qu’attendre la spécification parfaite. Vous êtes à l’aise avec les modèles de données, les bases de données et les API, et vous pouvez tenir une conversation technique. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être ingénieur·e, mais vous raisonnez comme tel·le, et vous êtes aussi à l’aise pour réfléchir à un modèle de données que pour penser à ce que l’utilisateur voit à l’écran

 Une communication claire et incisive, capable de faire le tri dans le bruit et d’expliquer la complexité tec

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 
 Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 
 Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 
 To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 
 BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 
 Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 
 
 
 The opportunity 
 Our engineering teams build a product that enterprises run their purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash processes on every day. Much of the product knowledge behind it sits with our founders and domain experts. As we grow, we are moving from a project-oriented model, where features come top-down and success is measured by output, to a product-oriented one: empowered teams that own problems end-to-end and are measured by their impact on customers and the business.
 As Head of Product, you lead that shift. You build the product management practice for the BLP Platform from an early stage. Our first product managers are joining stream-aligned teams, starting with Invoice and Procurement, and the team will grow to 4–5 PMs as we expand. You hire them, coach them, and set the standard for what great product work looks like at BLP.
 You report to the CTO and work closely with Engineering, Projects, Sales, and our founders.
 What you’ll do 
 Build and lead the product management practice for the BLP Platform: hire, coach, and develop a team of product managers as we scale.

 Move the product organization from an output-driven model to an outcome-driven one.

 Establish the product management craft at BLP: discovery practices, evidence-based decision making, and a clear standard for what “good” looks like in the role.

 Transfer product knowledge out of the experts’ heads and into the teams, without losing the domain depth that got us here.

 Build the direct line between our teams and our customers.

 Make our data usable for product decisions. We have BigQuery, PostHog, and prediction-rate analytics available, and we want product managers who reach for them by default.

 Shape how the product organization works as we grow: intake, prioritization, roadmapping, and the operating rhythm.

 Contribute directly to product strategy for the platform.

 What you bring 
 10+ years in product management, including experience leading or formally coaching product managers, with a real point of view on how product people are developed.

 Experience working in an empowered product model, where teams were assigned problems to solve rather than features to build.

jobs.description:
About BJAK 
 The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.
  
 Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.
  
 Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.
  
 We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.
  
 If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
  
 The Role 
 BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.
  
 This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. 
  
 We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.
  
 What you'll be doing 
 Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

 Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

 Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

 Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

 Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

 Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

 Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation. 
  

 What you'll need 
 Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

 Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

 Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

 AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

 Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

 Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap 

 Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch 

 Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds 

 AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted 

 Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

 Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

 To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

 We want to close that loop. If every car a dealer buys can go live on Carwow in hours, priced to sell and matched to the buyers who want it, we become the place dealers source, retail and sell their used stock. This role is the product voice at the table for that: setting the direction for a vertical we are fully investing in, and working day to day with design and engineering to build it.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - AI Team
jobs.description:
About us 
 Tebi is building a modern connected hospitality operating system that helps entrepreneurs run their business more intelligently and smoothly. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen, inventory, and payments (as well as all the data that powers it) helping to automate work, streamline operations, and give hospitality owners the clarity and time they need to focus on what matters the most: creating great guest experiences.
 Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is build in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Spain, Italy, Denmark, Germany, Finland, and Ireland.
 
 About the role 
 As the Senior Product Manager on our AI team, you'll own how AI shows up in Tebi, from an AI agent embedded in the product to the AI capabilities that run through the platform. Tebi sits on a unified foundation of sales, payments, reservations, kitchen and inventory data, which gives our AI something most restaurant software can't offer: the full picture. You'll own the vision, strategy and roadmap, and turn that data into agents and features that save merchants time, cut costs and help them make better decisions on a busy service.
 
 What you’ll do: 
 Define and own the vision and roadmap for Tebi's AI agent and AI capabilities across the product.

 Work with AI engineers and data teams to ship agentic features that take real actions for merchants, not just answer questions.

 Spend time with restaurant owners, managers and staff, plus Sales and Customer Success, to find the jobs where AI genuinely removes friction in their day.

 Define how we measure quality and trust in AI features, including evals, accuracy, adoption and merchant outcomes, and use that to iterate quickly.

 Decide where AI belongs in the product and where it doesn't, including guardrails, human-in-the-loop moments and when the merchant makes the final call.

 Partner with all the other product teams so AI feels native to Tebi rather than bolted on.

 
 What you'll need: 
 8+ years of product management experience at a fast-growing tech company, with a track record of shipping impactful launches.

 You are highly collaborative, able to partner effectively across the organization and build trust with both technical and operational teams.

 Hands-on experience building AI-powered products and a solid grasp of their strengths and limits.

 A data-driven mindset: you combine quantitative signals and qualitative feedback, and you know how to evaluate non-deterministic products.

 You care about the balance between craft, speed, and outcomes.

 This probably isn't the role for you if you're happiest on a structured environment with clear directions. We are looking for someone to set the direction and the vision for this team.
 People who succeed at Tebi are independent, curious and passionate about hospitality. If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers .
 
 Benefits: 
 Generous start-up equity

 Competitive Salary

 Lunch provided in the office

 Team building events

 Unlimited time off

 
 What is Restaurant Software? 
Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don't. It's a mess, and we are fixing it.
 From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it's a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.
 How We Use AI at Tebi 
We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.
 At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn't make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

The role 

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Agentic Search team, building the search and retrieval infrastructure that powers AI agents and LLM-based applications at scale.

You will work within a small PM team reporting to the Director of Product, alongside engineering, design, and go-to-market, shaping how AI agents discover, retrieve, and act on web information in real time.

The product serves both a developer-facing PLG motion and a growing enterprise customer base, so you will need to be equally comfortable digging into API design and search quality as you are running customer discovery calls and informing competitive positioning. We are looking for someone who can operate as a senior strategic partner, not just an executor, and who has the potential to grow into a principal-level PM over time.

You’re welcome to work hybrid from Tel Aviv, Israel.

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Own a core product area end-to-end: strategy, roadmap, execution, and iteration based on real usage signals and customer feedback.
  • Drive search quality and relevance improvements by working closely with engineering and research to define evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and release criteria.

  • Collaborate with go-to-market teams (sales, solutions, growth) to ensure product positioning, ICP definitions, and enablement materials reflect product reality.

We expect you to have: 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion in developer tools, API platforms, or search and retrieval infrastructure.
  • Track record of shipping products in fast-moving markets, working closely with engineering and design from concept through launch and iteration.
  • Strong understanding of LLMs, AI agents, and how search and retrieval systems fit into agentic workflows. Hands-on technical background is a strong plus.
  • Degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, with the ability to engage deeply with technical architecture and tradeoffs.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity: you can context-switch between strategic thinking and tactical execution without losing the thread.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

  • Experience in search, information retrieval, NLP, or adjacent domains.

  • Leadership experience in a high-growth technology company, especially post-acquisition or startup-within-a-larger-org environments.
  • People management or mentoring experience (building the skills of other PMs).

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.
 Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data.
 About Us
 Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing.
 Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo.
 The Role
 You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work.
 Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked.
 We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging.
 What You'll Do
 Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them.
 Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads.
 Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first.
 Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own.
 Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them.
 Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers.
 Hiring Process
 Application: your CV, plus a short answer about one metric you moved (what it was, what you shipped, what happened, and what didn't work)
 15-minute phone screen
 First interview (60 min): a deep dive into product growth work you've done. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo.
 Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem
 Culture fit (45 min)
 We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.
 Requirements 
 You Should Have
 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS : you were accountable for a metric for long enough to see whether your changes worked. In your application, tell us which metric it was, where it started and where it ended, what you shipped, and what didn't work.
 Product craft and taste : you love software and have used a lot of it yourself, so you know what a good product feels like. You keep scope small, work in short cycles with engineers and designers, run your own customer calls, and have well-reasoned opinions about UX.
 An AI-native way of working and building : you've shipped an AI-powered feature and measured whether people use it, you prototype with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), and you're happy to open a small PR yourself for something like a copy change.
 You do your own analysis : you write SQL, build funnels yourself, and know when a sample is too small to conclude anything.
 Experience with technical products : you've built for engineers or data teams and are comfortable talking about pipelines, warehouses, and APIs.

Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, 2 choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission.
 Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé.

 Une connaissance des enjeux techniques liés à l’architecture d’une plateforme logicielle et aux intégrations entre systèmes.

jobs.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Die Energiewirtschaft steckt mitten in der größten Transition ihrer Geschichte. Energieversorger, Netzbetreiber und Lösungsanbieter brauchen Software, die da mithält, und sie brauchen jemanden, der ihnen klar und glaubwürdig erklärt, warum epilot genau die richtige Plattform ist.
 Als Senior Product Marketing Manager bist du genau diese Stimme im Markt. Du gestaltest mit, wie wir epilot als zentrale, AI-native Plattform für die neue Energiewelt positionieren. Und du sorgst dafür, dass Marketing, Sales und Customer Success eine gemeinsame Geschichte erzählen.
 Product Marketing ist für dich das Fundament jeder Kommunikation und nicht nur der Lieferant für Slides und Battle Cards? Dann lies weiter.
 epilot ist das XRM für die Energiewirtschaft: Unsere Plattform verbindet nicht nur Kund:innen, sondern auch Partner, Installateure, Lieferanten und interne Teams. Über 200 Energieversorger und Netzbetreiber arbeiten bereits damit, und unser Team aus über 120 Menschen wächst weiter. Wenn du Teil dieser Journey sein und epilot an entscheidender Stelle voranbringen möchtest, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung!
 
 Das erwartet dich 
 Positionierung und Messaging der epilot Plattform liegen in deiner Verantwortung, für Energieversorger, Netzbetreiber und Lösungsanbieter. Produktfunktionen übersetzt du in Mehrwerte, die bei allen wichtigen Personas ankommen.

 Nah am Markt: In Sales-Calls, im Gespräch mit Kund:innen und auf Branchenevents erfährst du, was Energieversorger gerade umtreibt. Daraus hältst du ICPs, Personas und Wettbewerbsanalysen aktuell und machst sie zu Wissen, mit dem das ganze Unternehmen arbeitet.

 Produktkampagnen und Markteinführungen steuerst du inhaltlich, von der Story bis zu den Kernbotschaften, gemeinsam mit unserem Campaign & Growth Marketing. Auch die inhaltliche Qualität unserer Produktseiten und weitere produktnahe Inhalte liegt in deiner Verantwortung.

 Sales und Customer Success machst du sprechfähig: mit Pitch-Materialien, Argumentationshilfen, Einwandbehandlung und Trainings.

 AI-gestützte Workflows für Product Marketing baust du auf und entwickelst sie weiter, etwa für Persona- und Wettbewerbsanalysen, Messaging oder Sales-Materialien. AI ist für dich kein Knopfdruck: Die Logik dahinter entwickelst du selbst.

 Unsere Junior Product Marketing Managerin führst du fachlich und begleitest sie in ihrer Entwicklung.

 Strategy, Produktmanagement, Sales, Customer Success, Campaign & Growth sowie Event Marketing schätzen dich als Sparringspartner:in. 

 
 Das bringst du mit 
 Mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-SaaS-Marketing , idealerweise im Product Marketing. Positionierung und Messaging hast du schon selbst verantwortet.

 Komplexe Produkte verstehst du schnell und erklärst sie einfach. Dabei findest du die Worte, bei denen Zielgruppen nicken, und nicht die, die nur intern gut klingen.

 Strategisch denken und selbst anpacken gehören für dich zusammen. Ein Messaging-Framework entwickelst du ebenso gern wie eine Produktseite oder einen Sales-Pitch. Auf ein Briefing wartest du nicht: Wo es eine klare Story braucht, bringst du sie auf den Weg.

 AI-Tools nutzt du nicht nur. Am liebsten baust du eigene Workflows, statt dich auf fertige Lösungen zu verlassen.

 Neugier auf die Energiewirtschaft ist entscheidend. Branchenerfahrung oder Wissen über Energieprozesse ist ein großes Plus, wichtiger ist aber deine Lust, tief einzutauchen.

 Überzeugungskraft: Stakeholder bis hin zum C-Level gewinnst du mit klaren Argumenten. Außerdem macht es dir Freude, andere fachlich zu begleiten und weiterzuentwickeln.

 Sprachen: Stilsicheres Deutsch auf C2-Niveau ist ein Muss, denn dein Messaging muss im deutschen Markt sitzen. Dazu sprichst du fließend Englisch, unsere Unternehmenssprache.

 
 Das bieten wir dir 
 Flexibles Arbeiten: Remote arbeiten, wann immer es passt, und regelmäßig in Köln zusammenkommen, wenn persönlicher Austausch zählt.

 Die Möglichkeit, die erfolgreichste SaaS-Plattform auf dem Energiemarkt mit aufzubauen.

 Start-up-Mentalität: dynamische Atmosphäre und großartiger Teamspirit.

 Ein stark wachsendes Unternehmen mit offener Kommunikationskultur, motivierten Kolleg:innen, und internationaler Unternehmenskultur

 Exponentielle Lernkurve – epilot wächst rasant, selbiges erwarten wir von dir

 Einen zentralen und modernen Standort im Herzen von Köln mit coolen Cafés direkt um die Ecke

 Transparenz – Wir pflegen eine sehr flache und offene Unternehmenskultur, alles ist einsehbar und steht zur Diskussion.

 Regelmäßige Teamevents wie bspw. zu Karneval, das Sommerfest, Weihnachtsfeier, Company breakfast und noch viel mehr Gelegenheiten deine epilot:innen auch außerhalb der Arbeitszeiten kennenzulernen

 Sportangebote wie Urban Sports Club, ein Gym um die Ecke u.v.m.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
jobs.description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone
 Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.
 At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.
 I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.
 Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.
 That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.
 You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.
 — Grigory
 
Why Secfix exists
 Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.
 Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.
 We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.
 This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.
 
What you'll actually do in the first 3 months
 This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:
 Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.
 Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.
 Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.
 
What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?
 After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.
 You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.
 Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:
 Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

 Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

Your job is to understand these buyers better than anyone at Light, turn what you learn into positioning and proof our sales team can use, and build the playbook we follow to scale our go-to-market across the sector.

 Building the sales kit, from customer stories and demo narratives to objection handling and one-pagers, so our reps speak the sector’s language.

 Training sales reps and SDRs on the buyers, workflows and vocabulary of each segment, and joining customer calls to hear what lands.

 Bringing the sector’s requirements back to Product, and separating the needs that recur from the one-off requests.

 Giving demand generation and field marketing the insight, content and angles they need for sector campaigns and events, and tracking what turns into pipeline.

 What We Think* You’ll Need

When you apply, tell us about a segment you got to know from scratch: how you learned it, what you changed because of it, and how you helped Sales win there.

 Retire The ERP.
 Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers: automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.
 We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. We’re an early team defining a new software category. If you’re excited to modernise how the world runs money, one agentic workflow at a time, you’re in the right place.
 Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we’re building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.
 
 About The Role
 This is a hands-on product role reporting to the VP of Product Development. You’ll own Lead to Cash: everything between a signed deal and cash in the bank. That covers contracts, billing and invoicing, revenue recognition, payments, and credit control. You’ll set the roadmap for the area with the VP, and your discovery and judgement decide what actually ships.
 In Lead to Cash, the ledger has to keep up with whatever commercial terms each customer signs. A contract changes mid-term, and the invoices, deferred revenue and reporting all have to follow. A parent company wants one bill for a dozen subsidiaries. A customer’s Stripe setup doesn’t match how they actually sell. Every customer bills a little differently, and the product has to absorb those differences without turning into a pile of one-offs. You work out which problems are patterns worth building for and which aren’t, and you say so.
 Your stakeholders are engineers, designers, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Implementation, and the Financial Controllers, Finance Directors and CFOs who run their revenue on Light. Most of them are senior, technical and short of time. They expect you to keep up, and to be honest with them when a request would cost more than it’s worth.
 
 Key Responsibilities
 Own the Lead to Cash roadmap and its delivery, from discovery to go-live, and the metrics that show whether it’s working for customers

 Turn contract terms, pricing models and revenue recognition rules into product requirements engineers can build from

 Decide which customer requests become product and which don’t, and bring a clear recommendation to the VP of Product Development when the call is a big one

 Lead discovery with finance teams: sit with them through a billing run or a month-end close and find what’s slow, manual or wrong

 Work with Sales and Solutions Engineering on what gets promised to customers, before it’s promised

jobs.title: Insurance Product Manager / Underwriter (P&C)
jobs.description:
Most insurance product roles ask you to perfect one product in one market. This one asks you to build Europe’s SME insurance products: decide what we cover and who we insure, negotiate it with our carriers and get it live, market after market.

 Deep in the wording. Fast in the build. 

 About Insify 

 Insurance for entrepreneurs is still built the old way: one market at a time, wordings nobody reads, and cover that leaves out the very businesses that need it most.

 We're doing it differently.

 Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France, Germany and Ireland, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

 We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

 Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.

 What you’ll own in your first year 
 You won’t inherit a finished product shelf. You’ll build the engine that fills it.

 
 Build the product engine. Turn how we benchmark a market into a system: compare cover, limits and exclusions across local players, our Dutch home product and our other markets, so every new product starts from facts, not gut feeling.

 Make the call on cover. Decide what we cover, what we don’t and who we insure, and turn it into a proposal. The tools do the comparison; the judgment is yours.

 Get it signed. Take the proposal to our risk carriers and negotiate it. You know what to push on, what to let go and which clause will set off six red flags.

 Get it live. Adapt our wordings to each new market, run the legal review and launch. Less writing from scratch, more making one strong product fit the next market. Then track loss ratios, competition and customer feedback, and sharpen it.

 Build what doesn’t exist yet. In the markets where we double down, own custom products from the insurance side, including cover for the trades and businesses others decline.

 
 Who you are 
 You’re an insurance expert first and a builder second, but a real one.

 You have 5+ years hands-on in commercial P&C (Property & Casualty) at an insurer, MGA, (re)insurer or specialist broker, across underwriting, product and wordings, ideally for SMEs.

 You know what is covered, what isn’t and what should be . Hand you a wording from a market you’ve never worked in and you’ll spot the gaps within minutes.

 You’ve worked across more than one line, product or market , and you can apply what you know to a market you’ve never seen.

 You’ve sat at the table with insurers or capacity providers and know where the red lines are.

 You’d rather fix insurance than complain about it. Maybe you already tried: at an insurtech, an MGA, your own startup, or on the carrier side building products with insurtechs.

 You think like the customer : plain questions, fair cover, and no excluding everything just to be safe.

 You’re at home in Excel and data , and curious about what automation and LLMs can take off your plate. You don’t need to code; our product and tech teams build the digital journey with you.

 You work fluently in English ; German, French or Dutch is a big plus.

 What we offer 

 Real ownership. You decide what we cover and work directly with the MT, close to where decisions get made.

 Range. More products and markets in a year than most people see in a decade at an incumbent.

 A share in what we build. Equity, so you share in the value you build.

 A team that cares. We live by four values: Grit, Care, Impact and Entrepreneurship.

 Growth. Room to grow into leading our insurance product work as we add markets, plus an in-house coaching and leadership program.

 The package. Competitive salary package + 6% pension, holidays, well-being budget and rich social events (ski trip, summer and winter party).

 The basics, done well. Office in central Amsterdam, laptop, hybrid working. Relocation support.

 If you know insurance inside out and you’d rather build products than maintain them, we’d like to meet you. No cover letter needed.

Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

 

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
About Nabla 
 Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:
 Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.
 AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.
 Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.
 Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.
 About the Role
 The Product Marketing Manager will own how Nabla positions, launches, and drives adoption of the product with clinicians across their entire journey — from onboarding and activation through engagement and retention.
 This is product marketing where the message ships directly to the user. You own the narrative for every new feature launch, then own the in-app and email programs that turn that narrative into activation.
 You'll define the segmentation, write the positioning, ship the campaigns, and measure whether they actually moved adoption.
 Userpilot is in place, but everything around it still needs to be built: the activation and adoption strategy, in-app and email templates, segmentation, cohort analysis, the process with Product Marketing peers, CSM, PM, and Design, and the campaign calendar.
 This is a hands-on, highly operational PMM role. We need someone who lives in the tools, is data-driven, can test fast, structure the process, and turn usage insights into concrete positioning and messaging decisions.
 Userpilot is the first step. Over time, this person will take ownership of the full communication stack across email, in-app, and other channels. The role works extremely closely with Product Marketing peers, Design, PM, Data, and Product Ops.
 Nabla serves two distinct audiences, and lifecycle programs must work for both:
 Self-serve clinicians , who discover, activate, and adopt the product largely on their own. Here, automated email and in-app communication carries most of the relationship — your messaging is the go-to-market motion.

 Mid-market and enterprise health systems , managed by CSMs. Here the human relationship leads, and your programs must arm and reinforce the CSM — giving them timing, context, and content, never working around them.

 You'll design each lifecycle so the right channel leads for each segment. On top of this, healthtech is a highly regulated industry with demanding clients: every communication must meet a high bar for accuracy, security, and professionalism, while still feeling personal and useful to busy clinicians.
 
 Responsibilities
 Feature Launch Positioning & Activation 
 Own weekly in-app launch communication for new features, end to end and at a fast cadence

 Define the positioning and messaging for each release — what it is, why a clinician should care, what changes in their day

 Design the in-app experience (placement, format, flow) for each launch

 Validate messaging with Product Marketing peers, PM, and Design before shipping

 Launch on time and coordinate across the relevant teams

 Track performance (reach, engagement, adoption) for every launch and iterate quickly on results

 Stay highly reactive to the product roadmap, turning new releases into clear, well-timed clinician communication

 Lifecycle Strategy and Execution 
 Own the full lifecycle strategy across onboarding, activation, engagement, and retention, ensuring each stage of the practitioner journey is intentional, personalized, and measurable

 Tailor segmentation, messaging, and cadence to the distinct needs of each segment:
 For self-serve, build automated email and in-app programs that drive activation, adoption, and retention with minimal human touch

 For mid-market and enterprise, build programs that complement and support CSMs

 
 Direct and execute creative strategy for lifecycle channels — briefing, reviewing, and optimizing copy and design for brand consistency and message effectiveness

 Build and maintain a clear campaign calendar across functions

 Experimentation and Analytics 
 Lead a rigorous experimentation roadmap: A/B and multivariate testing of messaging, creative, cadence, segmentation, and value propositions

 Define and own lifecycle KPIs, building reporting frameworks and sharing regular performance insights with marketing and cross-functional leadership

 Partner with Data and Analytics on audience segmentation, behavioral signals, and AI-driven insights to enhance personalization at scale

 Turn cohort and usage insights into concrete messaging and product-marketing actions

 Cross-functional Collaboration 
 Collaborate with Product Marketing peers, Design, PM, Data, Product Ops, Clinical, and Brand to align lifecycle programs with broader business goals and the practitioner experience

 Establish a clear, repeatable process across Product Marketing, CSM, PM, and Design for planning and shipping campaigns
